newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hails Hebron deal, ready to send observers.
newsitem.headline: Italy hails Hebron deal, ready to send observers.

text.p: Italy is ready to send observers to Hebron as part of an international mission to ensure security for residents following Israel's deal with the PLO to withdraw from most of the city, the Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
It made the offer in a statement warmly welcoming the breakthrough agreement as an act of great courage by both sides and a boost for the overall Middle East peace process.
"The achievement of the accord crowns the commitment of those, like Italy, who have worked actively to support the peace process," the statement said.
"In line with such action, Italy is ready to contribute to the interposition force...which will be deployed in Hebron to guarantee the security of the city," it added.
Switzerland's cabinet also said on Wednesday that Swiss observers were ready to deploy in Hebron.
Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Turkey have also been asked by Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation to join the 180-strong mission of trained observers and administrators.
The mission is supposed to last three months, but can be extended by another three months.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat bowed to intense U.S. political pressure and clinched the long-delayed Hebron accord at an overnight summit.
They also agreed Israel would complete three further pullbacks in the West Bank over the next 18 months.

The Italian statement said the Hebron deal augured well for wider Middle East peace moves in 1997, adding that Italy hoped the agreement would also pave the way for an end to the closure of Israel's borders with areas of Palestinian self-rule.
